cards.explanation: The LORD promises to rebuild the fallen tent of David like it was long ago. He says, "In that day I will restore the fallen tent of David. I will repair its gaps, restore its ruins, and rebuild it as in the days of old…" (Amos 9:11). Gaps, ruins, all of it. I know what it's like to be a fallen thing, friends, and this is the best news a fallen thing can hear.

The answer is Edom's remnant and the nations bearing His name. The LORD says it is "…that they may possess the remnant of Edom and all the nations that bear My name…" (Amos 9:12). Edom's remnant is the part of Edom that is left. Then He adds the nations that bear His name, so the promise reaches past Edom.

The picture shows plowing starting before the reaping is done. The LORD says, "…the plowman will overtake the reaper and the treader of grapes, the sower of seed." (Amos 9:13). The plowman is already showing up while the reaper is still out working. The picture is one job running right into the next, friends.

The word is "inhabit." The LORD says, "I will restore My people Israel from captivity; they will rebuild and inhabit the ruined cities." (Amos 9:14). They don't just fix the buildings and wave at them from the road, friends. They move in and live there.

The answer is True. Listen to the verse: "They will plant vineyards and drink their wine…" (Amos 9:14). Planting and drinking go together here. That's a big turn from the earlier warning in Amos 5:11, where the vineyards were planted but the wine wasn't theirs to drink.

The promise is that they will never again be uprooted. The LORD says, "I will firmly plant them in their own land, never again to be uprooted from the land that I have given them…" (Amos 9:15). Firmly planted, friends, like a tree with roots that go all the way down. And the LORD is the one doing the planting.

The answer is False. The verse says "…never again to be uprooted from the land that I have given them…" (Amos 9:15). The LORD is the one who gave it. It's a gift, friends, not something they won for themselves.
